title: Noba textbook series: Psychology (modules)
authors: Module authors named on each module (e.g. Frances Friedrich; Kathleen B. McDermott and Henry L. Roediger III; Gregory Murphy)
R. Biswas-Diener and E. Diener (series editors, as given in module citations)
description: Free online psychology modules written by named researchers ('Teach and learn psychology for free.'). The catalogue's Cognition and Language, Learning and Memory, and Sensation and Perception groups include Attention; Categories and Concepts; Consciousness; Language and Language Use; Theory of Mind; The Unconscious; Judgment and Decision Making; Intelligence; Conditioning and Learning; Factors Influencing Learning; Forgetting and Amnesia; Memory (Encoding, Storage, Retrieval); Eyewitness Testimony and Memory Biases; Failures of Awareness: The Case of Inattentional Blindness; Vision; Hearing; Multi-Modal Perception; Sensation and Perception. A Psychology as Science group adds Research Designs, Statistical Thinking, The Replication Crisis in Psychology and related modules. Each module has learning objectives, sections, outside resources, discussion questions, vocabulary and references.
rightsNotes: Each module opened ends with a statement such as 'Attention by Frances Friedrich is licensed under a Creative Commons Attribution-NonCommercial-ShareAlike 4.0 International License.' The home page states the licence 'Creative Commons Attribution-NonCommercial-ShareAlike 4.0 International License' except where otherwise noted; footer '© 2026 Diener Education Fund'.

Licence agreement (nobaproject.com/license-agreement, 2026-10-31): 'DEF grants User a Creative Commons Attribution-NonCommercial-Share Alike 4.0 International License.' Users may modify the work consistently with that licence but not on the Noba website itself; DEF may revoke the licence on breach; content may change without notice. No statement on AI, machine learning or text mining was found.
Corniversity exercises are original; any adaptation of module text is labelled and shared under CC BY-NC-SA. Instructor materials were not examined.

browse-content catalogue: module titles grouped by topic (cognition, memory, perception and research-methods titles as in the description)

Attention (Frances Friedrich, University of Utah): What is Attention?; Selective Attention (the cocktail party, dichotic listening, models of selective attention: Treisman's attenuation model, late selection models, multimode model; subliminal perception); Divided Attention and Multitasking; cited as 'Friedrich, F. (2026)' in R. Biswas-Diener & E. Diener (Eds), Noba textbook series: Psychology

Memory (Encoding, Storage, Retrieval) (Kathleen B. McDermott and Henry L. Roediger III, Washington University in St. Louis): Varieties of Memory; Three Stages of the Learning/Memory Process; Encoding; Storage; Retrieval; Putting It All Together

Categories and Concepts (Gregory Murphy, New York University): Nature of Categories (fuzzy categories, borderline items, typicality); Category Hierarchies; Theories of Concept Representation (prototype and exemplar); Knowledge
limitations: Introductory modules written for undergraduate survey courses; depth is below a full cognitive-psychology textbook.
The catalogue has no working-memory module; reasoning appears only through Judgment and Decision Making and Intelligence (not opened).
Only three modules were opened; the other titles are known from the catalogue.
Module citation years follow the current site year (2026), not the original writing date; no version history is shown.
Images and videos inside modules may be third-party ('except where otherwise noted'); they were not audited.
